conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Magnetic Properties & Spin-Only Formula
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Magnetic Properties & Spin-Only Formula

summaryBox.title: Magnetic Moments
summaryBox.takeaway: μ_s = √(n(n+2)) BM where n is number of unpaired electrons. (n=1 ⟹ 1.73 BM, n=2 ⟹ 2.84 BM, n=3 ⟹ 3.87 BM, n=4 ⟹ 4.90 BM, n=5 ⟹ 5.92 BM).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SPIN-ONLY MAGNETIC MOMENTS
                     
   $n = 1 \implies \mu_s = \sqrt{3}  = \mathbf{1.73\text{ BM}}$   ($\text{Ti}^{3+}, \text{V}^{4+}, \text{Cu}^{2+}$)
   $n = 2 \implies \mu_s = \sqrt{8}  = \mathbf{2.84\text{ BM}}$   ($\text{V}^{3+}, \text{Ni}^{2+}$)
   $n = 3 \implies \mu_s = \sqrt{15} = \mathbf{3.87\text{ BM}}$   ($\text{V}^{2+}, \text{Cr}^{3+}, \text{Mn}^{4+}$)
   $n = 4 \implies \mu_s = \sqrt{24} = \mathbf{4.90\text{ BM}}$   ($\text{Cr}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{2+}$)
   $n = 5 \implies \mu_s = \sqrt{35} = \mathbf{5.92\text{ BM}}$   ($\text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{3+}$)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Paramagnetism**: Arises from unpaired electrons ($n \ge 1$). Paramagnetic species are attracted into external magnetic fields.
• **Diamagnetism**: Arises when all electrons are paired ($n = 0$). Diamagnetic species are weakly repelled by magnetic fields.
• **Spin-Only Magnetic Moment ($\mu_s$)**:
$$\mathbf{\mu_s = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM (Bohr Magnetons)}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Mechanisms of Color Origin: d-d Transitions vs. LMCT
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Mechanisms of Color Origin: d-d Transitions vs. LMCT
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ORIGIN OF COLOR IN d-BLOCK
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
  $d-d$ ELECTRONIC TRANSITIONS                                LIGAND-TO-METAL CHARGE TRANSFER (LMCT)
  Operates in ions with incomplete $d^{1-9}$ subshells.       Operates in $d^0$ ions with high metal oxidation states.
  ├── Ligand field splits $d$-orbitals ($t_{2g}$ & $e_g$).   ├── Electron transiently moves from Ligand ──► Metal.
  ├── Electron absorbs visible $\lambda$, promoting $t_{2g} \to e_g$.└── **Intense, deep coloration** (*No $d-d$ transition!*).
  └── Examples: $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ (Blue), $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ (Yellow), $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ (Green)└── Examples: **$\text{MnO}_4^-$ (Deep Purple)**, **$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ (Orange)**
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **$d-d$ Electronic Transitions**: Ligand fields split d-orbitals into $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ sets. Visible light absorption promotes electrons between split levels (e.g., $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ blue, $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ green).
• **Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer (LMCT)**: In $d^0$ systems with high metal oxidation states, color is caused by transient electron transfer from oxygen $2p$ to vacant metal $3d$ orbitals (e.g., $\text{MnO}_4^-$ intense purple, $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ orange).
• **Colorless Ions**: $d^0$ ($\text{Sc}^{3+}, \text{Ti}^{4+}, \text{V}^{5+}$) and $d^{10}$ ($\text{Zn}^{2+}, \text{Cd}^{2+}, \text{Hg}^{2+}, \text{Cu}^+$) lack incomplete d-orbitals and are colorless.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.3 Catalysis, Interstitial Compounds, & Alloys
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.3 Catalysis, Interstitial Compounds, & Alloys
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CATALYTIC, INTERSTITIAL, & ALLOY PROPERTIES

1. Catalysis: Variable oxidation states form intermediates (V₂O₅ in Contact process, Fe in Haber, Raney Ni, TiCl₄ + Al(C₂H₅)₃ Ziegler-Natta).
2. Interstitial Compounds: Non-metal atoms (H, C, N, B) trapped in voids (TiC, Mn₄N, Fe₃C, VH_0.56). Properties: non-stoichiometric, extreme hardness, high MP, retain metallic conductivity.
3. Alloys: Atomic radii differ by <15% (Hume-Rothery rules), enabling solid solutions (Brass [Cu-Zn], Bronze [Cu-Sn], Stainless Steel [Fe-Cr-Ni]).
conceptBreakdown.content: Transition metals excel as industrial catalysts, form non-stoichiometric interstitial compounds with retained electrical conductivity, and easily form homogeneous alloys due to similar atomic radii.

quickRevision: Color in d¹-d⁹ ions is from d-d transitions.
Color in d⁰ ions (MnO₄⁻, Cr₂O₇²⁻) is from Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer (LMCT).
d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions are colorless (no d-d transitions).
Interstitial compounds retain metallic conductivity and have high hardness/MPs.
